newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORINT ENDS STEADY VS DLR, STAYS 30 PIPS FROM BID.
newsitem.headline: FORINT ENDS STEADY VS DLR, STAYS 30 PIPS FROM BID.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed unchanged against the dollar on Friday as it tracked dollar/mark movements on international markets, dealers said.
The Hungarian unit ended the Friday session at 174.30/35 to one dollar, unchanged from its opening.

Speculation caused by the turbulent international markets was seen as only temporarily keeping the forint around 30 pips below the resistance level but some dealers said they expected more fluctuations over the coming weeks ahead of a rumoured cut in the crawling peg devaluation rate of the forint.

"I think we will see more fluctuations as there's some speculation that the central bank may change the crawling peg davaluation rate on April 1," said Peter Luczo of Inter-Europa Bank. "I expect to see it move in a range of zero to 50 pips below the bid until then."
Most analysts expect the NBH to cut the devaluation rate to 1.1 percent per month from the current 1.2 percent.
The Swiss franc accounting for half low 1.3 billion forints currency futures turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange.
The Swiss unit fell for most maturuties while the dollar rose. -- Duncan Shiels Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
